Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for the second essay! The two umpires make their way out to the centre followed by the players of Australia Under-19. They are joined by the two openers of Zimbabwe Under-19, Nathaniel Hlabangana and Panashe Taruvinga. Charlie Anderson will start with the new ball for Australia Under-19. Let's play...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

On the other hand, it was a bit of a disappointing inning for Zimbabwe Under-19, as their pacers failed to pick up early wickets but the spinner did a good job in the last 20 overs by striking regularly towards the second half of their bowling effort. They got their first breakthrough on the 19th over, all thanks to Brandon Sunguro. The bowlers were having a bit of trouble breaking the partnerships. But the spinners did a quality performance in the last 15 overs or so. At the end of the innings, Ryan Simbi and Brandon Sunguro picked up two wickets each for themselves. Matthew Schonken also chipped in with one.  The fielding of the team was decent too, but the bowling unit failed to make up the expectations of the cricketing fans. In the last two overs, the bowlers were way too substandard which cost them 30 runs. It will be a tough chase for the Chevron batters but anything can happen in this game.

Sam Konstas is in for a chat. He says that these were good conditions to bat on. Credits the way Harry Dixon and skipper, Hugh Weibgen batted and Tom Campbell for his late cameo. Mentions that adapting to the wickets has been challenging but this was a flat one. Says that he and Harry Dixon understand their game well and they try to keep it nice and simple. Shares that his mother is here to support him while his father and the two brothers are back home in Australia. Feels that 296 is a good score and backs his bowlers to defend the total.

A late flourish from Tom Campbell has Australia Under-19 finish on a high and they end up with 296 on the board! Having won the toss, every other skipper so far in the completion has opted to bowl but Hugh Weibgen made a surprising decision to bat first and their batters have vindicated that decision.  The batting unit had a lot of questions to answer after the performance against Namibia but this inning showed their class. The openers, Harry Dixon and Sam Konstas knocked a really firm and steady partnership off 91 runs but it ended on the 19th over. The skipper, Hugh Weibgen, came out to the middle at number 3 and held the situation pretty well and revived the strong partnership. Harry Dixon on the opposite end scored a half-century but his beautiful innings ended as he got dismissed on 89 runs, just 11 runs short of making the century. After that, the Aussies began to lose wickets in a flurry. But the partnership of 43 runs between Charlie Anderson and Tom Campbell, and a few blows of the latter at the end of the over helped the Aussies to score 296 runs to challenge the Chevron batters.

Scott Styris joins him and says that he likes the decision of Australia Under-19 to bat first. Feels that the pitch will be better to bat than what we have seen so far because it is a lot drier. Feels that it does not have the same moisture as some of the previous games but reckons that there will be early movement on offer. Shares that it might come on a little better onto the bat and advises the bowlers to bowl full and make the batters play.

The skipper of Zimbabwe Under-19, Matthew Schonken says he is happy as they were going with bowling anyway. He continues that the pitch looks really good to bat but he would still like to bowl first. He reckons that they will play with a bit more positive intent and will look for points in the group. Ends by saying they are going with the same team as the last game.

The captain of Australia Under-19, Hugh Weibgen says that they will bat first. Reckons that the pitch looks better from a batting perspective and it is a lot harder. Feels that there will be something in it with the new ball and they will have to go through that phase early on. States that they have the players to get the job done but there were a few nerves in the first game which led to a few tactical errors. Informs that they have had to make a couple of forced changes and a tactical change for this game.
